correctness.rationale: For each n>=2 the geometric K-fixed points of the matching complex are exactly convex combinations with equal barycentric coefficients on K-edge orbits; the explicit barycenters of the individually admissible orbit-matchings triangulate that locus PL. A vertical-edge orbit contains both vertically adjacent edges in a column, so is forbidden. Horizontal orbits split into nonconflicting outer-row and central-row families. Column reversal yields q=n/2 or q=(n-3)/2 permitted orbits per family for even or odd n, and within each family precisely consecutive orbit indices conflict. Hence the full fixed orbit complex is Ind(P_q disjoint union P_q); q=0 at n=3 gives the empty realization, whereas n=2 gives a simplex. The elementary two-contractible-piece cover gives Ind(P_q) ~= suspension Ind(P_(q-3)), with initial q=1,2,3 cases. Joining two path complexes supplies the claimed integral sphere dimensions or contractibility, with the first sphere occurring q>=2 and arbitrarily high dimensions. An independent reconstruction of all reflection-edge orbits and conflicts agrees for n=2..24. These bounded tests do not prove all widths or integral topology.
residual_risks: The empty complex convention at q=0 is essential and explicitly separated.
The interpretation must remain common geometric fixed points, not fixed vertices, coinvariant homology, or quotient space.
